name: Robinhood

summary.text: Robinhood is a U.S. retail brokerage whose largest revenue source has been payment for order flow from market makers such as Citadel Securities. In December 2020 it agreed to pay $65 million to settle SEC charges that from 2015 to 2018 it misled customers about this revenue and failed its duty of best execution, depriving customers of $34.1 million in aggregate even after accounting for zero commissions. In June 2021 FINRA ordered it to pay about $70 million, the regulator's largest penalty to date, and it listed on Nasdaq under the symbol HOOD in 2021.

facts.claim: On December 17, 2020 Robinhood Financial agreed to pay $65 million to settle SEC charges that from 2015 to 2018 it made misleading statements and omissions about how it made money, including omitting payment for order flow from its FAQ pages, and that it failed its duty of best execution; it settled without admitting or denying the findings.

facts.claim: The SEC found that Robinhood's inferior trade prices deprived customers of $34.1 million in aggregate even after accounting for the savings from not paying commissions, and that between October 2018 and June 2019 it falsely claimed in an FAQ that it matched or beat competitors' execution quality.

facts.claim: Robinhood agreed to retain an independent consultant to review its policies on payment for order flow, best execution and disclosure; its chief legal officer said the settlement related to historical practices that did not reflect Robinhood today.

facts.claim: On June 30, 2021 FINRA ordered Robinhood to pay about $70 million, comprising a $57 million fine and about $12.6 million in restitution, the largest penalty FINRA had levied.

facts.claim: Robinhood filed to go public shortly after the FINRA settlement and listed on Nasdaq under the symbol HOOD; reporting put payment for order flow at about 75% of its 2020 revenue and 81% in the first quarter of 2021.
